DINO Barangay Affairs LEGALITY OF THE USE OF THE PORTION OF SAP BENEFITS OF AN INTENDED RECEPIENT FOR THE PURCHASE OF FOODS THAT WILL ALSO BE GIVEN TO THEM (INCLUDING THE REMAINING SAP MONETARY BENEFITS FROM SAID PURCHASE) July 21, 2020 ACTION REQUESTED: For the SILG's clearance. For USBA's signature, if amenable, regarding the above-mentioned subject. REFERENCE: on the attached draft letter Letter dated 15 June 2020 from Milagrosa M. Lacap, Punong Barangay, Brgy. Sto Nino, Hagonoy, Bulacan seeking clarification regarding the above-specified subject.

THIS LEVEL'S COMMENTS AND/OR RECOMMENDATION: To begin with, it is worth reiterating that the Social Amelioration Program ("SAP"), mandated under Republic Act ("RA") No. 11469, otherwise known as the "Bayanihan to Heal as One Act", is a cash emergency subsidy program of the national government in order to assist Filipinos whose lives are greatly affected by the coronavirus ("COVID-19") pandemic. Accordingly, this level deems it imperative to stress that the law states that no one can deduct any fees from the government cash grants to the poor. In that regard, several government agencies, including this Department, and spearheaded by the Department of Social Welfare and Development ("DSWD"), have issued Joint Memorandum Circularsl, aside from its respective issuances, in order to ensure the proper, most efficient and most secure manner of implementation and distribution of such grant. In addition, programs and/or procedure of local government units must always be consistent with the policies of the national government as provided under Section 4(g) of RA No. 11469, to wit: SECTION 4. - xxx (g) Ensure that all Local Government Units (LGUs) are acting within the letter and spirit of all the rules, regulations and directives issued by the National Government pursuant to this Act; are im lementin standards of Communi Quarantine consistent with what the National Government has laid down for the subiect area. while allowing LGUs to continue exercisinq their autonomy in matters undefined bv the National Government or are within the parameters it has set: and are fully cooperatinq towards a unified cohesive and orderl implementation of the national policy to address COVID-19: xxx Correspondingly, it is this level's view that the barangay shall not implement an arrangement wherein it will be allowed to deduct a portion of the SAP cash assistance of any qualified recipient equivalent to the 1 Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, s. 2020 entitled, SPECIAL GUIDELINES ON THE PROVISION OF SOCIAL AMELIORATION MEASURES BY THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT, DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT, DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY, DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE, DEPARTMENT OF BUDGET AND MANAGEMENT, AND DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT TO THE MOST AFFECTED RESIDENTS OF THE AREAS UNDER ENHANCED COMMUNITY QUARANTINE; Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2, s. 2020, JOINT IMPLEMENTING GUIDELINES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SOCIAL AMELIORATION PROGRAM FOR THE SECOND (2ND) TRANCHE.

amount of food being sold in the barangay, as such kind of arrangement is an irregular implementation of the SAP program which is proscribed. Further, even taking into account that the recipient accedes to the barangay's program, we are of the view that it is unethical for the barangay, which is the office in-charge of distributing the assistance fund, to devise methods that will deduct the cash allotted for the qualified families. Moreover, this level would like to prevent a situation wherein the barangay will have unbridled discretion in determining the specific amount to be deducted depending on the price of the item purchased but with little to no chance at all to review whether the actual price of the food sold is actually commensurate with the deduction. Hence, this level is of the opinion that such arrangement is unlawful and is an attempt to circumvent the law. In view of the foregoing, this level would like to emphasize that under RA No. 11469, aside from admonition such as reprimand and/or issuance of show cause orders, appropriate charges against corrupt barangay officials may be filed and if found guilty of SAP-related irregularities, may be fined not less than Pl 0,000 and up to P2 million, or be jailed for two months, or both. They may also be perpetually disqualified from holding any elective or appointive position. A LLLS/32/17 . ROMEO P. NITEZ Director IV

DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.diig.com.ph 06 August 2020 PUNONG BARANGAY MILAGROSA M. LACAP Brgy. Sto Nino, Hagonoy, Province of Bulacan Dear Punong Barangay Lacap: This has reference to your letter dated 15 June 2020 seeking clarification as to the legality of the act of the barangay in deducting a portion of the Social Amelioration Program ("SAP") intended for qualified recipients for the purchase of food being sold by the barangay. To begin with, it is worth reiterating that the Social Amelioration Program ("SAP"), mandated under Republic Act ("RA") No. 11469, Otherwise known as the "Bayanihan to Heal as One Act", is a cash emergency subsidy program of the national government in order to assist Filipinos whose lives are greatly affected by the coronavirus ("COVID-19") pandemic. Accordingly, this level deems it imperative to stress that the law states that no one can deduct any fees from the government cash grants to the poor. In that regard, several government agencies, including this Department, and spearheaded by the Department of Social Welfare and Development ("DSWD"), have issued Joint Memorandum Circularsl, aside from its respective issuances, in order to ensure the proper, most efficient and most secure manner of implementation and distribution of such grant. 1 Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, s. 2020 entitled, SPECIAL GUIDELINES ON THE PROVISION OF SOCIAL AMELIORATION MEASURES BY THE DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT, DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT, DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY, DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE, DEPARTMENT OF BUDGET AND MANAGEMENT, AND DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT TO THE MOST AFFECTED RESIDENTS OF THE AREAS UNDER ENHANCED COMMUNITY QUARANTINE; Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2, s. 2020, JOINT IMPLEMENTING GUIDELINES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SOCIAL AMELIORATION PROGRAM FOR THE SECOND (2ND) TRANCHE.

In addition, programs and/or procedure of local government units must always be consistent with the policies of the national govemment as provided under Section 4(g) of RA No. 11469, to wit: SECTION 4. - xxx (g) Ensure that all Local Govemment Units (LGUs) are acting within the letter and spirit of all the rules, regulations and directives issued by the National Govemment pursuant to this Act; re im lementin standards f Communi Ouarantine consistent wifi what the National Govemment has laid down for üe subiect area. while allowing LGUs to continue exercisinq their autonomy in matters undefined bv the National Govemment or ace within the parameters it has set: and are fully cooperating towards unified cohesiv and rderl implementation of fie national policy to address COVID-19: xxx Correspondingly, we are of the view that the barangay shall not implement an arrangement wherein it will be allowed to deduct a portion of the SAP cash assistance of any qualified recipient equivalent to the amount of food being sold in the barangay, as such kind of arrangement is an irregular implementation of the SAP program. Further, even taking into account that the recipient accedes to the barangay's program, it is unethical for the barangay, which is in the office in-charge of distributing the assistance fund, to devise methods that will deduct the cash allotted for the qualified families. Moreover, we would like to prevent a situation wherein the barangay will have unbridled discretion in determining the specific amount to be deducted depending on the price of the item purchased but with little to no chance at all to review whether the actual price of the food sold is actually commensurate with the deduction. Hence, it is our position that such arrangement is an attempt to circumvent the law. In view of the foregoing, may we emphasize that under RA No. 11469, aside from admonition such as reprimand and/or issuance of show cause orders, appropriate charges against corrupt barangay officials may be filed and if found guilty of SAP-related irregularities, may be fined not less than P 10,000 and up to P2 million, or be jailed for two months, or

both. They may also be perpetually disqualified from holding any elective or appointive position. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: U Ls/LRALLD/32/17 Copy furnished.
